title: Finite Cycler
prompt: Create a class Cycler(items) that loops over a finite list forever when used with next() directly, BUT supports it = iter(c) producing an iterator that cycles. Implement it as an iterator whose __next__ wraps around using modulo.

tests.name: wraps around
tests.code:
from itertools import islice
c = Cycler(['a', 'b'])
assert list(islice(c, 5)) == ['a', 'b', 'a', 'b', 'a']

tests.name: empty cycler is iterable but yields nothing
tests.code:
from itertools import islice
assert list(islice(Cycler([]), 3)) == []
tests.hint: Guard the empty case to avoid ZeroDivisionError.
